∀ {S : Type*} [Finite S] (M : CoxeterMatrix S) (J : Set S),
  let W := CoxeterMatrix.Group M
  let cs := CoxeterMatrix.toCoxeterSystem M
  let Label := { p : W × Set S //
    Set.image (fun u : W => u * p.1) (CoxeterSystem.parabolic cs J : Set W) =
      Set.image (fun u : W => p.1 * u) (CoxeterSystem.parabolic cs p.2 : Set W) ∧
    CoxeterSystem.IsMinimalCosetRep cs p.2 p.1 }
  let component : Set S → S → Set S := fun I a =>
    { b | b ∈ Set.insert a I ∧ Relation.ReflTransGen
      (fun i j : S => i ∈ Set.insert a I ∧ j ∈ Set.insert a I ∧ i ≠ j ∧ M i j ≠ 2) a b }
  let crossing : Label → Label → Prop := fun p q =>
    ∃ (a : S) (ha : a ∉ p.val.2)
      (hD : Finite (CoxeterSystem.parabolic cs (component p.val.2 a))),
      (SimpleWallCrossings S W M cs p.val.2 a ha hD).2.2 p.val.1 = q.val
  ∀ p q : Label, Relation.ReflTransGen crossing p q
sourceReason: Explicit user direction selects the finite-rank geometric statement at https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/artin-tits-normalisers-2509-21915/item-lem-finite-wall-path-artin-tits-normalisers. The supplied defect report was checked and does not identify Lemma 3.20(3) or Remark 3.22 as defective statements. Finite rank is user-directed, not a reported correction. Label is Cham(J), identified with relative chambers by ChamberLabelling. Every intermediate label remains a chamber, and each step is the prescribed component-based SimpleWallCrossings map. Relation.ReflTransGen allows any finite sequence, including zero crossings for equal endpoints. Coxeter type and J remain arbitrary; finiteness is required only of each crossing component, not of W, W_J or W_{I∪{a}}.
